tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)
tasks.notes: Durable job queue — the backbone Phase 7 runs on. Lease/heartbeat/reclaim, business-window awareness, priority ordering, concurrency cap. PG-backed on todos_platform.

prep.what: Build the persistent job queue that all sweeper agents pull from — the backbone the entire Phase 7 depends on.
prep.understand: Without this, the sweeper is fire-and-forget: crashed workers leave jobs stranded forever and there's no backpressure. Key invariants: (1) atomic lease so only one worker holds a job at a time, (2) heartbeat so stale leases get reclaimed automatically, (3) window-awareness so jobs don't fire outside business hours, (4) priority ordering so blocking jobs jump the line, (5) concurrency cap so repos aren't flooded. Build on PG (`todos_platform`), following the atomic OCC pattern in `lib/pg-board-repository.ts`.
approach: Write a `db/migrate` for a `jobs` table: `id`, `repo_id`, `type`, `priority`, `payload` (jsonb), `status` (queued/leased/done/failed), `lease_expires_at`, `heartbeat_at`, `attempt_count`, `created_at`.

Implement `lib/queue.ts`: `enqueue(job)`, `lease(workerId, ttlMs)` (atomic `UPDATE … WHERE status='queued' … RETURNING`), `heartbeat(jobId)`, `reclaim()` (marks leased+expired back to queued), `complete(jobId)`, `fail(jobId, err)`.
Add window-awareness in `lease()`: return null if current time is outside the configured `[window.start, window.end]` — don't dequeue, just wait.
Write tests: concurrent lease race (two workers, only one wins), stale reclaim after simulated timeout, priority ordering, window blocks a job outside hours.
resources: `db/migrate.ts` — existing migration runner to model your new migration on
VPS PG: `todos_platform` database (Bun PG client or `psql` on azteam-vps)
`lib/repository.contract.ts` — test structure to model queue tests on
